analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In זֹאת אוֹת הַבְּרִית, “this is the sign of the covenant,” הַבְּרִית completes the construct phrase and identifies what the sign signifies.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders, singular construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God identifies the parties as himself, those he addresses, and “every living creature with you.” This identifies the covenant whose sign he gives as the covenant with Noah and all flesh.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state. The preceding construct noun אוֹת gives the phrase אוֹת הַבְּרִית, “the sign of the covenant.”
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

analysis.morphology: Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים identifies God as the speaker. In אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי נֹתֵן, “which I am giving,” אֲנִי supplies the first-person subject of the participle נֹתֵן.
analysis.morphology: Independent first-person common singular personal pronoun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God identifies the covenant sign and says אֲנִי נֹתֵן בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם, “I am setting [it] between me and you.” The repeated בֵּין identifies the parties between whom the sign is set, including every living creature.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively with אֲנִי. It has no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: put or set something in a place

analysis.evidence: God calls this אוֹת הַבְּרִית, “the sign of the covenant.” בֵּינִי names God as the first party, and the repeated preposition introduces the others: the people addressed and every living creature with them.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with a first-person common singular pronominal suffix referring to God, the speaker.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם ‘between me and you’, the repeated preposition identifies those addressed as a party to the covenant whose sign God is giving.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ precedes the preposition בֵינֵי ‘between’, which takes the second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם ‘you’.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: After בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם (“between me and you”), וּבֵין introduces כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה אֲשֶׁר אִתְּכֶם (“every living creature with you”), including those creatures among the parties to the covenant.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and” and prefixes the preposition בֵין, “between.”
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה אֲשֶׁר אִתְּכֶם, כָּל quantifies the singular phrase נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, extending the covenant to every living creature with the addressees.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.
